primitives.latex: $$|\xi(x, t) \times \xi(y, t)| \le C |x - y| \iff \sin \theta(x, y, t) \le c |x - y|$$

reasoning_traces.think:
The fundamental obstruction to proving global regularity lies in the mismatch between discrete computational grids and continuous vector fields. Numerical simulations track specific seed trajectories, which are measure-zero events, while the Millennium Prize demands a proof for almost every initial datum. The BKM criterion provides a necessary condition for smoothness but fails as a sufficient test because it only monitors a localized peak rather than the full directional evolution. The CFM condition attempts to quantify this directional coherence, but it remains a static requirement on high-vorticity sets rather than a dynamical mechanism generating blow-up. All three primitives reveal the same core failure: they describe what smoothness looks like after the fact, not how it might break down through active nonlinear interactions.
